final:
I checked all 5 reviewer issues against the code: 4 are correct and 1 is right about the bug but wrong about what it causes. I didn't change any code. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, and the file is valid JSON.

| # | Category | Verdict | Actionable | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | YES | `AccessTokenContext.java:73` null-checks `grantType` a second time, with the message for `rawTokenId`. So `rawTokenId` is never checked, and a null value would end up encoded as `onrtac:null`. |
| 1 | CORRECTNESS | PARTIALLY_VALID | YES | The grant check in `AssertEvents.java:483` is inverted: it returns `false` when the grant matches. But the claim that this makes the tests fail is wrong. Because of the bad indices in issue 2, it compares `"ta"` against the expected grant, which never matches, so the matcher always passes. The two bugs cancel out, and the grant type is never actually checked in the four event assertions. |
| 2 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | YES | `substring(3, 5)` should be `substring(4, 6)`. The encoder (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`) writes session type, token type, then grant, 2 characters each, and the decoder reads the grant with `substring(4, 6)` at line 81. |
| 3 | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL | The "4th char" comment describes the buggy index. The grant starts at index 4 (the 5th character), so fix the comment along with issue 2. |
| 4 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | YES | The Javadoc at `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30` says "3-letters shortcut". Every grant returns 2 characters (`ac`, `rt`, `cc`, `ro`, `pc`, `te`, `pg`, `ci`, `dg`), and the decoder rejects anything other than 6 characters of context (line 74). A 3-letter shortcut would break decoding. This text is left over from the first-commit format. |

Issues 1 and 2 have to be fixed together. Fixing only one of them makes the tests fail; fixing both makes the matcher actually check the grant type.
